correctness.rationale: For circular ladder n≥5, all induced connected triples are P3 because graph is 3-regular and triangle-free, yielding 6n triangles in the Alexander dual; complete 1-skeleton has C(2n,2) edges. Four-sets with all triples connected are exactly the n square four-cycles; a five-set would give 5·4=3e edge-incidence, impossible. To compute ∂2 over Z, the 2n horizontal-path columns have unique length-2 chord rows; each square contributes 3 independent mixed-triangle columns with unit determinant on rows AC,BD,AB. Their 5n×5n block minor has determinant ±1, while n independent square tetrahedron-boundary cycles force rank≤5n, hence exact rank and saturated image. They generate entire integral ker∂2, ∂3 is injective, so only H1(K)=Z^{C(2n,2)−(2n−1)−5n}=Z^{2n²−8n+1}. Alexander duality shifts it to H_(2n−4) of cut complex; its full (2n−6)-skeleton and homology plus Hurewicz/Whitehead imply wedge of spheres. Independent unit 3×3 determinant −1 and n=5..9 ranks 11,25,43,65,91 corroborate, not proof.

originality.rationale: Chauhan–Shukla–Vinayak Conjecture 4.6(ii) actually predicts the EXACT integral homology formula for C_n□K2 n≥5 and Table 5 tabulates finite cases; the formula as conjecture and numeric values are not new. However the primary source does not prove it, rule out torsion in all n, or establish wedge homotopy. Bayer et al. treat K_m□K2 (clique prisms) and Chandrakar et al. treat P2□Pn (nonperiodic grids). Complete infinite-parameter proof and sphere-wedge strengthening survive as best-knowledge originality.

value.rationale: The work proves a specifically published unsolved conjecture for all n≥5 and strengthens its predicted Betti ranks to an integral homotopy classification.
